Stretch or center plots in the available space

Source: R/size.R
stretch_x.Rd

A plot often has more space in a layout than its panel needs, e.g. a plot below a row of plots, or next to a taller plot. These functions let the plot take that spare space:

Usage

stretch_x(...)

stretch_y(...)

center_x(...)

center_y(...)

Arguments

...

ggplots, layouts, or lists of them.

Value

The modified plot or layout if one object was supplied, otherwise a list. Layout functions such as row() splice such lists, so add_right(stretch_y(p1, p2)) works.

Details

  • stretch_x() and stretch_y() stretch the panel to fill the spare width or height.

  • center_x() and center_y() keep the panel at its size and center the plot in the spare space, with equal room on both sides. Its tag stays at the edge of the space. Only spare space within the row, column or grid the plot sits in is used; a centered plot never makes that container wider or taller.

x and y refer to the horizontal and vertical direction of the figure. For plots with flipped coordinates, stretch_x() therefore stretches the plot's y axis. If several plots in a row or column take spare space, they share it equally.

Panel sizes themselves are set on the plot: with tidyplots::adjust_size() for tidyplots, or with theme(panel.widths, panel.heights) for plain ggplots (a single unit sets the total size of all facet panels; use e.g. unit(c(30, 30), "mm") for 30 mm per panel). These functions work for both. Layouts are modified recursively, i.e. all plots inside them are changed.

Examples

p1 <- dummy(name = "p1", color = "#0072B2")
p2 <- dummy(name = "p2", color = "#D55E00")
p3 <- dummy(name = "p3", color = "#009E73")
wide <- dummy(name = "wide", color = "#E69F00", width = 50)

column(p1, p2) |>
  add_right(stretch_y(p3))


row(p1, p2) |>
  add_below(stretch_x(p3))


# keep the panel size, center the plot in the spare width
row(wide, wide) |>
  add_below(row(p1, center_x(p2))) |>
  layout_tags("A")
